samples.summary: Page Setup dialog's room check (`>= pageWidth`) is looser than `assertUsablePageSetup`'s (`> width - MIN_CONTENT_PX`), so a value in the sub-pixel band submits and throws an uncaught RangeError out of the React submit handler
samples.evidence: Dialog: `parsed.left! + parsed.right! >= pageWidth` (line 145) / `>= pageHeight` (147). Editor: `if (margins.left + margins.right > width - MIN_CONTENT_PX) throw new RangeError(...)` in `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts ~line 995). For any page dimension that is not an integer — e.g. a `paperSize.width` of 700.5 arriving from a collaborator's CRDT write via `YorkieDocStore.readPageSetup`, which does `Number(ps?.width)` with no rounding — margins summing to 700 pass the dialog (700 < 700.5) but fail the assert (700 > 699.5). `handleSubmit` calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` with no try/catch (line 154), so the RangeError escapes the form's onSubmit. The new editor test at packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:290 documents exactly this band ('refuses a setup the resolver would silently rescale'), but the only production caller does not honour it.

samples.summary: `formatSourcePosition` falls back to the run *before* the selection whenever an endpoint is not a top-level context block (e.g. a drag from a paragraph end into a table cell) — the exact mis-pick the function was written to prevent
samples.evidence: `const endIdx = blocks.findIndex((b) => b.id === normalized.end.blockId);` searches `this.doc.getContextBlocks()`, which contains only top-level blocks, not blocks nested inside table cells. Dragging from the end of a paragraph (`start.offset === startLen`, so the `< startLen` fast path at line 436 is skipped) into a table cell gives `endIdx === -1`; `endIdx >= startIdx` is false, the forward walk is skipped entirely, and the function returns `{ blockId: normalized.start.blockId, offset: normalized.start.offset }` (line 459) — which `caretInlineStyle` resolves to the start block's *last* run, i.e. the run immediately preceding the selection. Same happens when the *start* block is a cell block (`startIdx === -1`). The user sees one format highlighted and copies another.

samples.summary: `URI_CHARS` / `ENTITY_REFERENCE` silently drop legitimate link and image targets from the Markdown export (link degrades to bare text, image to `[image]`)
samples.evidence: `URI_CHARS` admits only the strict RFC 3986 set plus non-ASCII, so a real-world URL carrying `|`, `{`, `}`, `^` or `"` — e.g. `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto|Open+Sans`, which browsers accept verbatim — fails `isLiteralDestination` and the link is emitted as plain text with no diagnostic. `ENTITY_REFERENCE = /&(?:#[0-9]+|#[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]+|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);/` additionally drops any URL whose query happens to contain `&name;`, e.g. `https://x/?a=1®b=2`. Silent data loss in an export path; a percent-encoding normalization for the rejected characters (rather than dropping) would preserve the link.

samples.summary: `pasteFormat()` takes an undo snapshot and reports `true` even when nothing is actually written, producing an empty undo step
samples.evidence: `pasteFormat()` returns `true` unconditionally after `this.saveSnapshot(); this.applyStyleToSelection(...)` (lines 480-484). `applyStyleToSelection` may write nothing — e.g. a selection consisting only of structural inlines (image / pageNumber runs), or a buffer whose values already match every target run. The caller `EditorAPI.pasteFormat` then fires `notifyStyleApplied()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts ~2982) and the undo stack gains an entry that reverts nothing, so the user's next Ctrl+Z appears to do nothing. The read-only test at packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts asserts `snapshots).toHaveLength(0)` for the refused case, showing the author cares about this invariant on the other branch.

samples.summary: Routing the parsed DOCX geometry through `resolvePageSetup` measures the landscape margin fit against the wrong axis, because the parser stores already-swapped `w:pgSz` dimensions while `getEffectiveDimensions` expects portrait-relative ones
samples.evidence: A landscape `.docx` carries `<w:pgSz w:w="16838" w:h="11906" w:orient="landscape"/>` — width and height already swapped. `parsePageSetup` stores those verbatim as `paperSize.width/height` *and* sets `orientation = 'landscape'`. `resolvePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:841-843) then computes `width = paperSize.height` and `height = paperSize.width`, i.e. swaps a second time, so `fitMargins` clamps the left/right pair against the page's *height* and vice versa. The double-swap itself predates this change (`getEffectiveDimensions` has the same convention mismatch, and `buildSectPrXml` writes the stored dims back raw), but the new `resolvePageSetup` call makes the import's clamp inherit it. Impact is limited to landscape imports whose margins are near the page bound.

samples.summary: `resolvePageSetup` is not idempotent at the clamp boundary: floating-point scaling can leave `near*scale + far*scale` fractionally above `extent - MIN_CONTENT_PX`, so each subsequent read shrinks the margins again
samples.evidence: `const scale = Math.max(0, (extent - MIN_CONTENT_PX) / total); return [near * scale, far * scale];` — the sum of the two scaled values is not guaranteed to be `<= extent - MIN_CONTENT_PX` in floating point, so a re-resolve of the clamped result can re-enter the scaling branch. Every read path (editor render, ruler, exporters) calls this on each pass, and `ruler.onMarginChange` re-stores the resolved value, so a document sitting exactly at the boundary can drift by ULPs. Also means `getPageSetup()` may not `toEqual` the geometry that was just stored.

finding.summary: The new `resolvePageSetup` clamp is bypassed by the PDF and DOCX exporters, which read `doc.pageSetup` raw — so the unusable geometry the clamp exists to neutralise still reaches them
finding.evidence: `resolvePageSetup`'s new docstring (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:796-802) asserts it is "the single read path — the editor, the ruler, `MemDocStore`, `YorkieDocStore`, the CLI's pagination and PDF export all reach the page setup through it". That is false for the exporters: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:87` does `const setup = doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP;` and then `getEffectiveDimensions(setup)` / `paginateLayout(layout, setup)` at :88-92, and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:162` does `buildSectPrXml(doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP, ...)`. Neither calls `resolvePageSetup`. The value they read is exactly the unvalidated one the clamp was added for: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:530-543` (`readPageSetup`) builds `document.pageSetup` with `Number(ps?.width)` / `Number(m?.top)`, which is `NaN` for a missing or non-numeric CRDT field, and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:53` hands precisely `editor.getStore().getDocument()` to the PDF/DOCX exporters. Result: a partially-written or hostile `root.pageSetup` yields NaN page width/height and NaN margins in the exported PDF (NaN `x`/`y`/page sizes) and `w:w="NaN"` in the exported .docx — a corrupt file, produced silently.

verdict.reason: The finding claims neither exporter calls resolvePageSetup and that both read doc.pageSetup raw. Both do call it: packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:96 does `const setup = resolvePageSetup(doc.pageSetup);` and feeds that resolved value into getEffectiveDimensions (:97), contentWidth (:98) and paginateLayout (:101); packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:168 does `buildSectPrXml(resolvePageSetup(doc.pageSetup), ...)`. Imports at pdf-exporter.ts:11 and docx-exporter.ts:3. The quoted raw reads (`doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` at pdf:87 / docx:162) are not in the tree — those lines are comments explaining that the raw read was removed because YorkieDocStore.readPageSetup can yield NaN. The docstring at types.ts:800-825 likewise names both exporters as callers rather than excluding them, and resolvePageSetup (types.ts:826-849, via usableSize/usableMargin/fitMargins) clamps NaN before it reaches pdf-lib's addPage or <w:pgSz>. So the NaN-to-corrupt-file path the finding asserts is already closed.
